candidates.description: Presence of CDKN2A gene alteration, specifically homozygous deletion or loss.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Identify mentions of CDKN2A in molecular profiling sections; mark as positive if 'homozygous deletion' or 'loss' is specified.
candidates.measurement_definition: Detected via next-generation sequencing (NGS) as 'homozygous deletion' or 'loss'. Positive indicates the presence of the deletion/loss; negative indicates wild-type or no documented alteration.
candidates.name: CDKN2A status
candidates.uncertainty: The evidence uses both 'homozygous deletion' and 'loss'; it is uncertain if these are treated as equivalent for all clinical interpretations.

citations.quote: ECOG performance status remains 2 (ambulatory, capable of self‑care but unable to carry out work activities)
ECOG 3 (limited self‑care, confined to bed >50% of waking hours)

candidates.description: A scale used to assess the functional status of the patient and their ability to perform activities of daily living.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the numeric value associated with 'ECOG' or 'performance status'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Numeric score from 0 (fully active) to 4 (completely disabled), as documented in clinical notes.
candidates.name: ECOG Performance Status
candidates.uncertainty: Variable timing of measurement (baseline vs. progress notes) may introduce measurement bias.

limitations: The evidence is limited to a small number of specific case excerpts.
Genomic reporting terminology is slightly inconsistent (e.g., 'deletion' vs 'loss').
summary: The evidence identifies baseline genomic alterations (specifically CDKN2A loss) and functional status (ECOG Performance Status) as distinct clinical variables associated with patients presenting with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer and brain metastases.
